name: Bauhaus (supplemental design reference; not a directly named source style)
visualIdentity: Circles, squares, triangles, rules, and lettering are composed on a shared grid. Asymmetric balance relies on deliberate proportions. Forms are assembled in rhythmic stages through growth, rotation, and interlocking. The source states that not every primary-color geometric animation is Bauhaus.
suitableUses: Explicitly listed good fits are UI and product storytelling, editorial and minimalist layouts, and motion posters with staged geometric compositions. Inferred from the combinations guidance are logo reveals, design-education pieces, and brand section transitions. Suitability for other topics is unspecified.
limitations: Adapt or omit the style when recomposition changes hierarchy without explaining the subject. Avoid it when an anchored subject crops important details or when pinning breaks layout. Grid size, 120 BPM, and 20 beats are optional starting parameters, not defining features. The source does not confirm that every suggested detail was verified in a video.
palette: Suggested tokens are not supplied exact colors: background #FFFFFF, foreground #000000, accent_1 #D62828 red, accent_2 #F2C230 yellow, accent_3 #164B9B blue. Gradients are disabled, so flat fields stay discrete. Two-color contrast is 21:1 for foreground on background, 5.008:1 for background on accent_1, 12.535:1 for foreground on accent_2, and 8.354:1 for background on accent_3. Approved exact colors override these, and composited frames must be checked.
motionAndInteraction: Assembly proceeds in rhythmic stages using growth, rotation, and interlocking forms. Motion is driven by seekable composition time, not wall-clock playback. Optional timing uses 120 BPM, so each beat lasts 0.5 seconds and 20 beats last 10 seconds. Deliberate sharp cuts and reading holds should be preserved, since not every transition needs easing. Interactive behavior is unspecified for the base style.
audio: The source specifies no required soundtrack or voice for the base style. Audio is a task-specific suggestion, and music is optional. A beat-event table can synchronize music to assembly stages when music is used. Speech must stay intelligible, and clipping must be avoided. Autoplaying sound is listed as something to avoid in the timing combination.
assetRequirements: No asset files are listed for the base style, so asset needs are unspecified. The task must supply subject, exact copy, duration, aspect ratio, resolution, frame rate, and output location. Fonts and any local assets must load before rendering begins. Audio must be authorized or created separately. The motion-pattern catalog is optional, and no motion reference is required.
combinations: Explicitly suggested: style-100 for morphing among circle, square, and triangle states, using SVG and GSAP, with morphs limited to primitives and color changes snapping rather than blending. Also suggested: style-105 as a timing-only engine driven by a verified beat table for music-backed loops. Bauhaus alone suits posters and primitive-based identities. The five primary tokens must stay fixed when combining styles.
productionApproach: HyperFrames is the default pipeline for composition, timing, audio sync, validation, and export. Remotion is a conditional fallback only when HyperFrames is unavailable or a verified limitation exists, and the reason must be recorded. SVG is the suggested style renderer for geometry and text positions, with p5.js optional for procedural layers. GSAP is the suggested motion engine, with Motion or Anime.js optional under single-property ownership. chroma.js can validate colors. Decoded frames and seek tests must be verified.
